def add_bmll_source(fig):
    if not hasattr(fig, 'add_annotation'):
        return fig
    existing = getattr(fig.layout, 'annotations', None) or ()
    if any(getattr(a, 'name', None) == '_bmll_source' for a in existing):
        return fig
    fig.add_annotation(
        name='_bmll_source', xref='paper', yref='paper', x=1.0, y=0.0,
        xanchor='right', yanchor='top', yshift=-60, showarrow=False,
        text='Source: BMLL',
        font=dict(color=BMLL_PRIMARY_BLUE, size=11, family='Inter, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif'),
    )
    return fig

def apply_bmll_plotly_style(fig, *, show_source=True):
    if hasattr(fig, 'update_layout'):
        fig.update_layout(
            font=dict(family='Inter, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif', color='#1a1a1a'),
            colorway=BMLL_CYCLE,
            paper_bgcolor='white',
            plot_bgcolor='white',
            margin=dict(l=80, r=40, t=80, b=90),
        )
        fig.update_xaxes(showgrid=True, gridcolor='#ECECEC', zerolinecolor='#DADADA')
        fig.update_yaxes(showgrid=True, gridcolor='#ECECEC', zerolinecolor='#DADADA')
    if show_source:
        add_bmll_source(fig)
    return fig

SECTION 1 BMLL Notebook Educational Series
### Closing Auction Imbalance & Price Formation

The closing auction is the most important event of the trading day: a large fraction of daily volume executes at the official closing price, making it the primary benchmark for passive funds, index products, and TCA benchmarks.

Exchanges publish a continuous feed of auction imbalance data throughout the closing call period, revealing:

  • The indicative uncrossing price — where the book would cross if the auction ended now
  • The paired quantity — how much volume has been matched at the indicative price
  • The imbalance quantity — the surplus of buy or sell orders that cannot be matched
  • The reference price — the exchange's anchor price (often the last mid-price)

Tracking how these metrics evolve during the auction helps participants:

  • Detect one-sided liquidity pressure and anticipate price direction
  • Time participation orders to maximize fill probability
  • Understand venue-specific auction dynamics

Note: This analysis covers venues that publish transparency data during the auction (e.g., LSE/XLON, Euronext/XPAR, NYSE/XNYS, NASDAQ/XNAS). Not all venues publish intraday imbalance feeds. For the price dislocation chart, three fallback tiers are used: (1) exchange-published reference price, (2) auction BBO mid-price, (3) first indicative uncrossing price of the day as an auction-open anchor.

import datetime as _dt
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

Configuration¶

  • MIC: Market Identifier Code for the exchange (e.g., XLON, XPAR, XNYS)
  • Ticker: Exchange ticker as reported by the venue
  • Date range: Analysis period — imbalance patterns are averaged across all trading days

Venues with well-populated closing auction imbalance data include: XLON (LSE), XPAR (Euronext Paris), XAMS (Euronext Amsterdam), XETR (XETRA), XMIL (Borsa Italiana), XSWX (SIX Swiss), XNAS (NASDAQ), XNYS (NYSE).

Step 1: Load Closing Auction Imbalance Data¶

Reference price note: Not all venues populate REFERENCE_PRICE in the imbalance feed. Where it is absent we fall back to the auction mid-price (BEST_BID_PRICE + BEST_ASK_PRICE) / 2, which the exchange reports when the book is not yet fully crossed. If neither is available the value is carried forward from the previous snapshot within the same day so that charts remain continuous.

Explore a closing auction¶

Load AZN's closing-auction updates on XLON for 2026-08-25, then chart how the indicative price, paired quantity and imbalance evolve towards the close. Add up to five session dates to compare auctions. Prices use the reported currency unit. This short sample focuses on individual auction dynamics.

In [11]:
def prepare_auction_query(raw, session_date):
    """Map a projected API session to the shared auction analysis columns."""
    if raw.empty:
        raise ValueError(f"No closing-auction observations for {session_date}")
    if not raw["MarketState"].eq("CLOSING_AUCTION").all():
        raise ValueError("Unexpected market-state values in closing-auction query")
    if raw["CurrencyCode"].isna().any() or raw["CurrencyCode"].nunique() != 1:
        raise ValueError("Expected one non-null currency unit per session")
    # BMLL AuctionImbalanceSide: 1 bid, 2 ask, 3 none, 4 insufficient orders.
    side_map = {0: "UNKNOWN", 1: "BID", 2: "ASK", 3: "NONE", 4: "INSUFFICIENT_ORDERS", -1: "UNKNOWN"}
    sides = raw["ImbalanceSide"].astype(object).replace(side_map)
    if sides.isna().any() or not sides.isin(["BID", "ASK", "NONE", "UNKNOWN", "INSUFFICIENT_ORDERS", "HALTED"]).all():
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported imbalance sides: {raw['ImbalanceSide'].unique()}")
    frame = raw.rename(columns={
        "TradeDate": "TRADE_DATE", "LocalTimestamp": "LOCAL_TIMESTAMP",
        "Timestamp": "TIMESTAMP", "BMLLSequenceNo": "BMLL_SEQUENCE_NO",
        "MarketState": "MARKET_STATE", "ImbalanceSide": "IMBALANCE_SIDE",
        "ReferencePrice": "REFERENCE_PRICE", "IndicativeUncrossingPrice": "INDICATIVE_UNCROSSING_PRICE",
        "PairedQuantity": "PAIRED_QUANTITY", "ImbalanceQuantity": "IMBALANCE_QUANTITY",
        "CurrencyCode": "CURRENCY_CODE",
    }).copy()
    frame["IMBALANCE_SIDE"] = sides
    frame["TRADE_DATE"] = pd.to_datetime(frame["TRADE_DATE"]).dt.date
    # The API tags wall-clock LocalTimestamp values as UTC: drop that tag,
    # preserving the exchange-local hour, rather than converting it again.
    frame["LOCAL_TIMESTAMP"] = pd.to_datetime(frame["LOCAL_TIMESTAMP"]).dt.tz_localize(None)
    frame["TIMESTAMP"] = pd.to_datetime(frame["TIMESTAMP"], utc=True)
    if frame[["LOCAL_TIMESTAMP", "TIMESTAMP", "BMLL_SEQUENCE_NO"]].isna().any().any():
        raise ValueError("Missing auction timestamp or sequence number")
    if not frame["TRADE_DATE"].eq(_dt.date.fromisoformat(session_date)).all():
        raise ValueError("Query returned observations from another session")
    ref = pd.to_numeric(frame["REFERENCE_PRICE"], errors="raise")
    bid = pd.to_numeric(frame["BestBidPrice"], errors="raise")
    ask = pd.to_numeric(frame["BestAskPrice"], errors="raise")
    frame["REFERENCE_PRICE"] = ref.where(ref > 0).fillna(((bid + ask) / 2).where((bid > 0) & (ask > 0)))
    for col in ["INDICATIVE_UNCROSSING_PRICE", "PAIRED_QUANTITY", "IMBALANCE_QUANTITY"]:
        frame[col] = pd.to_numeric(frame[col], errors="raise")
    if not (frame["INDICATIVE_UNCROSSING_PRICE"] > 0).any():
        raise ValueError(f"No valid indicative prices for {session_date}")
    return frame.sort_values(["TIMESTAMP", "BMLL_SEQUENCE_NO"], kind="stable")

Step 2: Intraday Auction Dynamics¶

We aggregate all closing-auction snapshots by time-of-day (in 5-second bins) to reveal the typical evolution of the auction across the selected sessions.

Key metrics tracked:

  • Price dislocation (bps): (indicative_uncrossing_price − reference_price) / reference_price × 10,000
  • Imbalance quantity: Excess buy or sell volume that cannot be matched
  • Paired quantity: Volume successfully matched at the indicative price
In [14]:
if df_raw.empty:
    print("No data found for the specified parameters.")
else:
    df = df_raw.copy()

    # Ensure LOCAL_TIMESTAMP is datetime
    df["LOCAL_TIMESTAMP"] = pd.to_datetime(df["LOCAL_TIMESTAMP"])

    # ── Reference price: three-tier fallback ─────────────────────────────────
    # Tier 1 (SQL): exchange-published REFERENCE_PRICE, or auction BBO mid when absent.
    # Tier 2 (Python): carry the last known value forward/backward within each day
    #   so that sparse publication (e.g., only the first snapshot) fills all rows.
    # Tier 3 (Python): if the venue publishes neither, anchor on the first valid
    #   INDICATIVE_UNCROSSING_PRICE of the day (dislocation then measures movement
    #   relative to the auction open rather than a pre-auction mid).
    df = df.sort_values(["TRADE_DATE", "LOCAL_TIMESTAMP"], kind="stable")

    # Zero → NaN so pandas fill functions treat them uniformly
    df["REFERENCE_PRICE"] = df["REFERENCE_PRICE"].replace(0, np.nan)

    # Tier 2: ffill then bfill within each day
    df["REFERENCE_PRICE"] = (
        df.groupby("TRADE_DATE")["REFERENCE_PRICE"]
        .transform(lambda s: s.ffill().bfill())
    )

    # Tier 3: still missing → use first valid indicative price as per-day anchor
    _using_indicative_anchor = df["REFERENCE_PRICE"].isna().any()
    if _using_indicative_anchor:
        first_indicative = (
            df[df["INDICATIVE_UNCROSSING_PRICE"] > 0]
            .groupby("TRADE_DATE")["INDICATIVE_UNCROSSING_PRICE"]
            .first()
        )
        df["REFERENCE_PRICE"] = df["REFERENCE_PRICE"].fillna(
            df["TRADE_DATE"].map(first_indicative)
        )
        print("Note: reference price not available for this venue — "
              "using first indicative uncrossing price as per-day anchor "
              "(dislocation = movement relative to auction open).")

    # Keep only rows with a valid indicative price (required for all analyses).
    df = df[df["INDICATIVE_UNCROSSING_PRICE"].notna() & (df["INDICATIVE_UNCROSSING_PRICE"] > 0)]

    if df.empty:
        raise ValueError("No valid indicative prices for the selected parameters")

    # Price dislocation from reference price (in basis points)
    df_with_ref = df[df["REFERENCE_PRICE"].notna() & (df["REFERENCE_PRICE"] > 0)].copy()
    df_with_ref["price_dislocation_bps"] = (
        (df_with_ref["INDICATIVE_UNCROSSING_PRICE"] - df_with_ref["REFERENCE_PRICE"])
        / df_with_ref["REFERENCE_PRICE"]
        * 10_000
    )

    # Time-of-day in seconds since midnight (for cross-date aggregation)
    for _d in [df, df_with_ref]:
        _d["tod_seconds"] = (
            _d["LOCAL_TIMESTAMP"].dt.hour * 3600
            + _d["LOCAL_TIMESTAMP"].dt.minute * 60
            + _d["LOCAL_TIMESTAMP"].dt.second
        )
        _d["tod_bin"] = (_d["tod_seconds"] // 5) * 5

    # Quantity aggregation over all rows with a valid indicative price
    avg_qty = df.groupby("tod_bin").agg(
        avg_imbalance_qty=("IMBALANCE_QUANTITY", "mean"),
        avg_paired_qty=("PAIRED_QUANTITY", "mean"),
        n_days=("TRADE_DATE", "nunique"),
    ).reset_index()
    avg_qty["time_label"] = pd.to_datetime(avg_qty["tod_bin"], unit="s", origin="1970-01-01").dt.strftime("%H:%M:%S")

    # Dislocation aggregation — only where reference price is available
    avg_dis = pd.DataFrame()
    if not df_with_ref.empty:
        avg_dis = df_with_ref.groupby("tod_bin").agg(
            avg_dislocation=("price_dislocation_bps", "mean"),
            p25_dislocation=("price_dislocation_bps", lambda x: x.quantile(0.25)),
            p75_dislocation=("price_dislocation_bps", lambda x: x.quantile(0.75)),
        ).reset_index()
        avg_dis["time_label"] = pd.to_datetime(avg_dis["tod_bin"], unit="s", origin="1970-01-01").dt.strftime("%H:%M:%S")

    print(f"Analysis covers {avg_qty['n_days'].max()} trading days")
    print(f"Auction time window: {avg_qty['time_label'].iloc[0]} — {avg_qty['time_label'].iloc[-1]}")

Note: reference price not available for this venue — using first indicative uncrossing price as per-day anchor (dislocation = movement relative to auction open).

Plot 1: Price Dislocation During the Closing Auction¶

Indicative price dislocation shows how far the auction's tentative execution price strays from the reference price. As the auction proceeds and more orders arrive, this dislocation typically narrows toward zero — signalling convergence to the final price.

Wide sustained dislocation indicates strong directional flow; tight convergence suggests balanced order flow.

if not df_raw.empty and not avg_dis.empty:
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5))

    ax.fill_between(
        avg_dis["tod_bin"],
        avg_dis["p25_dislocation"],
        avg_dis["p75_dislocation"],
        alpha=0.2,
        color="steelblue",
        label="25th–75th percentile",
    )
    ax.plot(avg_dis["tod_bin"], avg_dis["avg_dislocation"], color="steelblue", linewidth=2, label="Mean")
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.8, linestyle="--", alpha=0.5)

    _ref_label = "Auction-Open Anchor" if _using_indicative_anchor else "Reference Price"
    ax.set_xlabel("Local time (HH:MM:SS)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Price dislocation (bps)")
    ax.set_title(
        f"Closing Auction: Indicative Price Dislocation from {_ref_label}\n"
        f"{ticker} on {mic}  |  {start_date} – {end_date}"
    )

    # X-axis: show every ~60 seconds
    tick_step = max(1, len(avg_dis) // 10)
    ax.set_xticks(avg_dis["tod_bin"].iloc[::tick_step])
    ax.set_xticklabels(avg_dis["time_label"].iloc[::tick_step], rotation=30, ha="right")

    ax.legend()
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
elif not df_raw.empty:
    print("Price dislocation chart skipped — reference price not available for this venue/ticker.")

Plot 2: Imbalance and Paired Quantity Over Auction Time¶

As closing auction participants see the imbalance feed, they tend to send orders to offset the surplus side. This typically leads to:

  • Rising paired quantity as more volume is matched
  • Falling imbalance quantity as the surplus is absorbed

if not df_raw.empty and not avg_qty.empty:
    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5))

    ax1.plot(avg_qty["tod_bin"], avg_qty["avg_paired_qty"], color="green", linewidth=2, label="Avg paired quantity")
    ax1.set_ylabel("Paired quantity (shares)", color="green")
    ax1.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor="green")

    ax2 = ax1.twinx()
    ax2.plot(avg_qty["tod_bin"], avg_qty["avg_imbalance_qty"], color="red", linewidth=2, linestyle="--", label="Avg imbalance quantity")
    ax2.set_ylabel("Imbalance quantity (shares)", color="red")
    ax2.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor="red")

    ax1.set_xlabel("Local time (HH:MM:SS)")
    ax1.set_title(
        f"Closing Auction: Order Matching vs. Imbalance Over Time\n"
        f"{ticker} on {mic}  |  {start_date} – {end_date}"
    )

    tick_step = max(1, len(avg_qty) // 10)
    ax1.set_xticks(avg_qty["tod_bin"].iloc[::tick_step])
    ax1.set_xticklabels(avg_qty["time_label"].iloc[::tick_step], rotation=30, ha="right")

    lines1, labels1 = ax1.get_legend_handles_labels()
    lines2, labels2 = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
    ax1.legend(lines1 + lines2, labels1 + labels2, loc="upper left")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

Step 4: Single-Day Drill-Down¶

For a deeper look at price formation dynamics, we plot one representative day to show how the indicative price, reference price, and imbalance evolve minute-by-minute through the closing auction.

Show technical code
In [23]:
if not df_raw.empty:
    # Pick the day with the most imbalance data as the representative day
    day_counts = df.groupby("TRADE_DATE")["LOCAL_TIMESTAMP"].count()
    representative_day = day_counts.idxmax()
    day_df = df[df["TRADE_DATE"] == representative_day].sort_values("LOCAL_TIMESTAMP", kind="stable")

    print(f"Representative day: {representative_day}  ({len(day_df)} snapshots)")

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(12, 8), sharex=True)

    # Price evolution
    axes[0].plot(
        day_df["LOCAL_TIMESTAMP"], day_df["INDICATIVE_UNCROSSING_PRICE"],
        label="Indicative uncrossing price", color="steelblue", linewidth=1.5,
    )
    axes[0].plot(
        day_df["LOCAL_TIMESTAMP"], day_df["REFERENCE_PRICE"],
        label="Reference price", color="grey", linewidth=1.5, linestyle="--",
    )
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Price")
    axes[0].set_title(
        f"Closing Auction Price Formation — {representative_day}\n{ticker} on {mic}"
    )
    axes[0].legend()

    # Imbalance quantity and paired quantity
    axes[1].fill_between(
        day_df["LOCAL_TIMESTAMP"], 0, day_df["PAIRED_QUANTITY"],
        alpha=0.4, color="green", label="Paired quantity",
    )
    axes[1].plot(
        day_df["LOCAL_TIMESTAMP"], day_df["IMBALANCE_QUANTITY"],
        color="red", linewidth=1.5, label="Imbalance quantity",
    )
    axes[1].set_ylabel("Quantity (shares)")
    axes[1].set_xlabel("Local time")
    axes[1].legend()

    for ax in axes:
        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%H:%M:%S"))
        plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=30, ha="right")

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
